McLaren: McLaren’s aero package has been tweaked all over the car – the front and rear corner pods, side‑pod inlets and even the rear wing now have fresh “furniture” to smooth airflow, while a new floor shape adds extra grip. They’ve also swapped in circuit‑specific side‑pod louvers to keep the engine cooler under the weekend’s hot conditions. In short, the changes give the car cleaner air and more downforce where it counts, boosting stability and speed for the upcoming race.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has shifted the rear‑pipe and fitted a new slotted bracket, which trims the car’s drag and should give a touch more straight‑line speed. At the front, they’ve tweaked the edge of the front wing end‑plate, smoothing the air around the front wheels for better grip when turning. Those two tweaks are aimed at getting a bit more top‑end speed and more stable corner entry for this weekend’s race.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull have tweaked almost every aero‑section for the weekend – the front wing and rear corner now have reshaped elements to give the car a steadier, more balanced grip, while the side‑pod inlet, floor and engine cover have been smoothed to improve airflow around the car’s underside. The rear wing’s deployment mechanism has also been refined for more reliable straight‑line performance. All these changes aim to boost cornering stability and straight‑line speed, giving the team a better chance to fight for podium spots at this circuit.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has given the front wing a sharper bite with a new end‑plate channel and extra vane, while reshaping the front corner and suspension fairings to smooth the air onto the car’s floor.  A series of tweaks to the floor, diffuser and rear wing—including extended edge scoops, re‑profiled tail devices and a revised beam‑wing connection—tighten the rear aero pack and cut drag, giving more stable grip through the high‑speed corners of this weekend’s circuit.  In short, the updates are all about getting cleaner airflow and extra downforce where it counts, so the team can attack the track with better balance and pace.
Williams Racing: Williams has re‑sculpted the floor, side‑pods and rear‑body panels to fit the car’s new layout, tightening up the airflow under the car and across the top for a cleaner, more efficient aerodynamic package. The mirror housings, tail‑pipe bracket and the fairings around the rear‑impact structure have all been reshaped and repositioned, while the rear‑brace wing has got fresh cut‑lines, giving the rear end a smoother flow path and better cooling. In short, the updates should give the car a bit more down‑force and stability this weekend, especially through high‑speed corners and heavy braking zones.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls have reshaped the rear‑corner area and its surrounding suspension fairings to smooth airflow, while the rear wing and its endplates now sport fresh profiles that increase down‑force without adding drag. The front wing gains an extra flap setting and refined endplates, and the floor‑edge slots, forward floorboard and diffuser have been tweaked with new strakes and winglets to boost overall grip. All these tweaks should give the car a tighter aerodynamic balance and more usable rear‑end stability, helping the team extract extra lap‑time on this weekend’s circuit.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin did not submit any updates for this event.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has tweaked the rear diffuser’s load settings, giving the car a bit more rear‑end grip and a smoother airflow off the back of the car. The change should help the team generate a little extra downforce on the straights and through fast corners, which can translate into better straight‑line speed and more stability in the high‑speed sections of this weekend’s circuit. In short, the tweak is aimed at shaving off a few tenths of a second and giving the drivers a more confident feel on the track.
Audi F1 Team: Audi’s new front brake duct and revamped suspension leg covers smooth the airflow around the front wheels, giving the car a tighter, more stable feel into the corners. Meanwhile, a reshaped floor edge, updated diffuser and a fresh winglet boost the car’s down‑force, helping it stick to the track and improve straight‑line speed. Together, these tweaks should make the car more predictable and quicker on both the high‑speed sections and the twisty parts of this weekend’s circuit.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has tweaked a handful of aero‑parts and the rear suspension to tighten up the car’s airflow and give the driver a bit more stability on the straights and through the corners. The new front‑drum exit and revised nose‑camera mounts smooth the front‑end flow, while a reshaped rear‑wing and endplate plus a reinforced rear impact structure add extra rear‑end grip and balance. All of these changes should translate into cleaner aerodynamics and a more predictable car on this weekend’s circuit, helping Alpine push harder in qualifying and fight for better race positions.
